chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Vocalist Edd Battles and knowing the old standards
summary: Edd Battles of Philadelphia has a fine vibrato and knows lyrics to every standard, helping Horace when middle-class patrons challenge the band with old tunes.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And I had heard Hawk and the other guys do these things, and I tried to pass this knowledge on to the other guys, you know, and it worked out real well. But now we're going to get back into my group again. I have other guys to talk about. I've had several vocalists in my group at different times, but I've got a boy with me right now named Edd Battles, and he's out of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. And I would say Edd was pretty close to 40 years of age, but this guy is uncanny. He has an excellent vibrato. He sings beautifully.
And the thing that knocks me out, though, he -- for his age, he knows the lyrics to all of the old tunes, the standards.
Like if you want to go back to things like Anytime and Oh, Eva with Fater (unintelligible), and
like last night there was a guy came up and asked for the Blue Danube Waltz. He knew the lyrics to this.

Yeah, and he's always going around to the different music stores, buying up books, old books and everything with all the lyrics, and he knows all the tunes, which is a help, you know, and he plays a little guitar, not in the band, but at home he practices on one string. He can pick the melody out, you know, and he teaches himself these things. You don't have to sit down and teach him a tune, you know.
And a guy like that is helpful to the leader.

Yeah. So I'm very proud of these guys. We just have a ball at night, he's helpful, and like the place we're playing now, more or less a group that we're getting all this clientele that -- I won't say the elderly, but they're middle class (unintelligible), like all the old standards. And then they call sometimes -- when we volunteer or we make a statement, rather, over the microphone, "Is there anything special you folks would like for us to play, one of those things, and nine times out of ten they're the old ones say, Bet you don't know these tunes. Bet you don't know this tune, and so on. So Eddy will whisper over to me, I know it if you do." "If you don't."
And my goodness, man, sometimes I have to go to

my little library, because if it's a 32 bar thing, you might know the first eight bars sometimes, and the bridge might have slipped you, your (unintelligible) memory. So sometimes they pays to get forget it, you know. I told the guys sometimes -- I make them laugh. I said, "I tell you, if we get to playing something sometime, one of these old ones, Sweet Sue is always in the key of G. Let's go, and (unintelligible) fall out, you know.
Yeah, use the stock bridge or something.
